title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election for Ohio's 3rd Congressional District
description: The 2026 general election for Ohio's 3rd Congressional District pits incumbent Democratic Rep. Joyce Beatty against Republican business owner Cleophus Dulaney and independent candidate Michelle Bird. The district, anchored in Columbus and Franklin County, was redrawn under Ohio's mid-decade redistricting in October 2025 but remains a safely Democratic seat according to major election forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball). Beatty, first elected in 2012, is seeking a seventh full term and chairs or has chaired the Congressional Black Caucus. Dulaney, who ran unopposed in the Republican primary, previously ran for this seat in 2020. Bird, running as an anti-corruption independent, collected enough signatures to qualify for the general election ballot.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found specifically for the 2026 general election in Ohio's 3rd Congressional District as of mid-2026.

candidates.name: Joyce Beatty
candidates.summary: Joyce Beatty is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Ohio's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2012 and serving since 2013. She previously served in the Ohio House of Representatives (1999–2008) and was Senior Vice President for Outreach and Engagement at Ohio State University. Beatty is a former chair of the Congressional Black Caucus and focuses on voting rights, economic development, healthcare, and education.

candidates.name: Cleophus Dulaney
candidates.summary: Cleophus Dulaney is the Republican nominee for Ohio's 3rd Congressional District, running unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary. He is a long-time Columbus resident, business owner (New Image Furniture), and community servant who previously ran for this congressional seat in 2020. Dulaney's campaign focuses on affordable housing, tax relief, police-community relations, and support for small businesses.

candidates.name: Michelle Bird
candidates.summary: Michelle Bird is an independent candidate for Ohio's 3rd Congressional District, running on an anti-corruption platform focused on ending dark money in politics, promoting peace, and restoring power to the people. She submitted over 3,040 signatures to qualify for the November 2026 general election ballot, exceeding the required 2,492. Her campaign is called 'Michelle Bird for Ending Dark Money.'

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling was found as of mid-2026, which increases uncertainty. However, the race description explicitly states that all three major nonpartisan election forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball) rate this seat as safely Democratic after the 2025 redistricting. Incumbent Joyce Beatty is a seven-term incumbent, former chair of the Congressional Black Caucus, and represents a Columbus/Franklin County-anchored district with a strong Democratic lean. The Republican nominee, Cleophus Dulaney, ran unopposed in the primary and previously lost this seat in 2020. Independent Michelle Bird is running an anti-corruption campaign but faces structural disadvantages as a third-party candidate in a safely Democratic seat. Given the expert ratings, incumbency, and district partisan baseline, Democrats have an overwhelming advantage, though confidence is medium due to the absence of public opinion polling.
